data.text: Everything needed is in hand. Summary of what the evidence shows:

data.reason: The firewall's WAN interface driver (vtnet0, VirtIO) has wedged: dmesg shows repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link down/up cycles, and the stack can no longer hand packets to the NIC (ENOBUFS), so nothing reaches the ISP even though the modem re-registered and reports OPERATIONAL.

data.cause: The firewall's WAN interface driver (vtnet0, VirtIO) has wedged: dmesg shows repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link down/up cycles, and the stack can no longer hand packets to the NIC (ENOBUFS), so nothing reaches the ISP even though the modem re-registered and reports OPERATIONAL.
evidence: dmesg -a: four 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' entries interleaved with 'link state changed to DOWN/UP' — the NIC queue repeatedly stalls and the link bounces.
ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1: 'ping: sendto: No buffer space available', 100% loss — transmit path into the NIC is stuck, not a routing/firewall drop.
arp -n: gateway entry '(198.51.100.1) at (incomplete)' while the WAN address itself is present — ARP cannot complete because frames never leave the hung queue.
netstat -i: vtnet0 Oerrs 48211 with Ierrs 0 — persistent transmit errors on that NIC only; vtnet1 (LAN) is clean, matching 'local services still work'.

netstat -rn: default route via 198.51.100.1 on vtnet0 is intact, and /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0 shows a valid lease (fixed-address 198.51.100.27, expire 2026/3/6), so addressing/DHCP is not the fault.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json + events.jsonl: outage_start ~02:01-02:06, four WAN reloads during this outage all rc=0, then at 03:30 'action none, reason reload_cap (12/12 in 24h)' — interface reloads did not restore traffic, so a further wan_reload will not clear a driver-level hang.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl + modem-metrics.jsonl: 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' 02:01:44 then 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete' 02:28:21, cm_status OPERATIONAL since — the provider side recovered; the outage persists only on the firewall's NIC.
data.recommendation: Reboot the firewall (gw.lan) to reset the wedged vtnet0/VirtIO device and its queues; a wan_reload has already been tried four times in this outage (and the 24h cap of 12 reloads is reached) without effect, and the modem is registered/OPERATIONAL so a modem reboot would not help. Afterwards, check for a virtio driver/firmware update or NIC replacement if watchdog timeouts recur.
data.detail: vtnet0 (VirtIO WAN NIC) transmit queue hung — repeated watchdog timeouts
